newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Balkan natgas demand seen up at 36-37 bcm in 2010.
newsitem.headline: Balkan natgas demand seen up at 36-37 bcm in 2010.

text.p: Bulgarian-Russian joint gas stock company Topenergy said on Wednesday it sees natural gas demand in the Balkans increasing to 36-37 billlion cubic metres (bcm) annually by the year 2010.
The company did not give any figures for current demand.

The demand forecasts for the Balkans do not include Romania, Bosnia, Croatia and Slovenia, Topenergy's Galina Pavlova said in a report at a meeting of the European Union's Energy Centre on natural gas infrastructure development in Bulgaria.
Topenergy, in which Russia's gas giant Gazprom holds a 50-percent stake, plans to sell and deliver Russian gas to the Balkans via Bulgaria.
"Plans are to transit Russian natural gas through the territory of Romania and via Bulgaria it will be distributed...to the borders of Turkey, Greece, Macedonia and Serbia," the report said.
Topenergy plans annual supplies of Russian gas in 2010 of 20 bcm for Turkey, four bcm for Greece, one bcm for Albania, two bcm for Serbia and one bcm for Macedonia, Pavlova said.
The Bulgarian government is expected to award a concession in mid-October for the construction of pipelines to Topenergy, which was established in May last year.

Sasho Donchev, who is on the Topenergy board and is also an executive direator of Bulgaria's private gas distribution firm Overgas pointed out that with its geographical position Bulgaria had the opportunity "to become a transitting gas corridor from Russia to the Balkans and Italy".

Bulgaria has a 2,200-km pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country. But Topenergy needs to enlarge the transit pipeline to 1,300 km by 2010 and build 240-megawatt compressor stations to meet the growing Balkan demand, Pavlova said.
The firm plans to increase the Bulgarian distribution system from 17 bcm to some 30 bcm.
Bulgaria expects its 1996 demand to be more than six bcm in 1996 and forecasts a rise up to eight percent by the year 2000.

Topenergy is also to build gas storage facilities in Bulgaria over the next 10-15 years with a capacity of 3.5-4 bcm in order to ensure constant supplies to the Balkan countries. It already has the Chiren storage facility in northern Bulgaria.
